newsitem.title: CANADA: Shell Cda moves Coral to top 5 gas firms.
newsitem.headline: Shell Cda moves Coral to top 5 gas firms.

text.p: Houston-based Coral Energy LP would move into the ranks of the top five North American natural gas megamarketers with the addition Shell Canada Ltd's production, a Shell spokeswoman said.

The deal announced on Monday would see Coral, a partnership of Royal Dutch Shell Group U.S. unit Shell Oil Co and Tejas Gas Corp, market Shell Canada's 800 million cubic feet per day of gas production starting by the end of this year.
Coral would then market a total of about six billion cubic feet per day of gas across North America.
Shell's Tara Black said in an interview that under the deal, which is still subject to final approval, Shell would take a minority stake in Coral.

Black declined to say the amount Shell Canada expected to save by moving its gas marketing activities into Coral. Shell Canada currently employs about 15 marketers, most of whom are expected to work in Coral's planned Calgary office.
"Admittedly, we won't have the overhead, but this isn't a cost-reduction exercise, this is a value-add exercise," she said.
The largest North American gas marketers include NGC Corp -Chevron Corp, Enron Corp and Mobil Corp -PanEnergy Corp.
Westcoast Energy Inc and Coastal Corp were also reported to be discussing a major natural gas marketing merger.
Analysts have said the merger wave is being driven by a need to compete with growing firms that cover a widening market area and handle more trading and financial services.
"We see the opportunity to serve the customers better," Black said. "It's becoming a very competitive market and a very North American market."
She said no financial details were being made public before the deal gets the final green light.
Shell Canada is Canada's fourth-largest gas producer behind Amoco Corp unit Amoco Canada Petroleum Co Ltd, Petro-Canada and PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd.
